note: agent-lifted from VC's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: Fabric outage
concepts.gloss: An interruption of a digital cross-connect's switching fabric at some point on an ODU route that causes the tributary's customer service to fail.
concepts.example: A VC-DXC fabric stops switching an ODU, so the attached tributary raises TRIB-FAIL and the customer service drops.

concepts.label: Mis-provisioned connection
concepts.gloss: An incorrectly configured cross-connect connection that sends an ODU to the wrong destination and thereby disrupts its tributary service.
concepts.example: After provisioning, an ODU intended for tributary A is switched to tributary B, producing TRACE-MISMATCH and a service failure.

concepts.label: Tributary failure
concepts.gloss: An outage of the tributary path or endpoint that prevents the customer service carried by that tributary from operating.
concepts.example: A failed tributary interface cuts the customer's service even though the optical line remains operational.

concepts.label: any fault
concepts.gloss: A deliberately nonspecific fault anywhere on the active, primary, standby, or end-to-end path that can account for a route-related alarm.
concepts.example: ON-STANDBY is attributed to any fault on the primary ODU route until a more specific cause is identified.

concepts.label: the tributary
concepts.gloss: A fault attributable to the tributary equipment or connection at either end of the customer service rather than to an intermediate route element.
concepts.example: TRIB-FAIL is traced to the customer-facing tributary at the remote endpoint.

concepts.label: tributary hardware fault
concepts.gloss: A physical equipment failure within the local tributary interface that triggers a tributary hardware condition.
concepts.example: A failed circuit on a VC-TRIB-100 raises TRIB-HW against that tributary.

concepts.label: fabric hardware fault
concepts.gloss: A physical failure within the local digital cross-connect fabric that prevents normal ODU switching.
concepts.example: A switching-card failure in the VC-DXC raises FABRIC-HW against the cross-connect.

concepts.label: Amplifier outage
synonyms: the module is out of service
concepts.gloss: A complete loss of operation of an optical fibre amplifier, causing its outgoing aggregate light to disappear and affecting downstream wavelengths.
concepts.example: A mid-span VC-OFA-M loses power, emits no light, and raises OUT-DARK while the next amplifier reports IN-DARK.

concepts.label: Gain sag
concepts.gloss: A degradation in which an optical amplifier's gain falls below its configured value, weakening and degrading all wavelengths it carries.
concepts.example: A landing OFA loses 3 dB of gain, so every outgoing channel is 3 dB weaker and GAIN-DEV is raised.

concepts.label: Excess noise
concepts.gloss: Excess optical noise introduced by an earlier amplifier that degrades every carried wavelength even when measured power levels remain normal.
concepts.example: An upstream OFA adds ASE noise, leaving channel power unchanged but lowering OSNR and eventually causing FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: Pump wear-out
concepts.gloss: Slow ageing of an optical amplifier pump that progressively raises required pump drive and culminates in an end-of-life indication.
concepts.example: I-PUMP rises from 100% to 121% of its commissioning value over several months, causing PUMP-EOL.

concepts.label: Spectral tilt
concepts.gloss: A band-dependent optical degradation in which amplifier gain varies across the spectrum, preferentially weakening wavelengths at one end of the band.
concepts.example: Channels at the long-wavelength edge leave an OFA 2 dB weaker than channels near the band centre.

concepts.label: a severed fibre
concepts.gloss: A physical break in a feeding fibre span or earlier route segment that removes incoming optical and supervisory signals.
concepts.example: Construction cuts the fibre before a mid-span OFA, which then raises IN-DARK and SV-LOSS.

concepts.label: fibre attenuation that has jumped
concepts.gloss: A sudden increase in loss on a feeding fibre span or upstream route segment that sharply reduces received optical power.
concepts.example: A newly bent cable adds 10 dB of loss, causing DEGRADE and then FRAME-LOSS at the terminal.

concepts.label: an unplugged patch lead
concepts.gloss: A disconnected patch lead at the start of a wavelength section that interrupts light for all downstream elements on that route.
concepts.example: A technician unplugs the launch patch cord, and the remote terminal raises RX-DARK.

concepts.label: Over-attenuation
concepts.gloss: Optical loss beyond the wavelength router's compensation range that leaves an individual wavelength weak at the router output.
concepts.example: A channel arrives 11 dB low where the router can compensate only 8 dB, so it exits 3 dB below launch level.

concepts.label: Passband misalignment
concepts.gloss: Misalignment between a wavelength and a router filter passband that clips the signal and degrades quality despite a normal measured level.
concepts.example: A shifted WSS filter clips one channel, whose power looks normal but whose pre-FEC error ratio rises.

concepts.label: Direction input fault
synonyms: a router input that has failed
concepts.gloss: Failure of one directional input of a wavelength router that blocks all light entering on that direction while traffic from other directions continues.
concepts.example: The east input card fails, stopping all eastbound incoming channels at the router while north and west channels pass normally.

concepts.label: Transmitter dark
concepts.gloss: A remote wavelength transmitter outage in which its laser emits no light, leaving the receiving terminal dark.
concepts.example: The far-end VC-WT-400T laser switches off, and the local terminal raises RX-DARK.

concepts.label: Module failure
concepts.gloss: A hardware outage of a wavelength terminal module that loses its transmitted and received traffic, stops telemetry, and masks subordinate traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A VC-WT-400A module fails, raising MOD-HW, stopping telemetry, and removing its wavelength in both directions.

concepts.label: Receiver impairment
concepts.gloss: A local terminal receiver degradation that creates pre-FEC errors on that receiver while the route and other wavelengths remain healthy.
concepts.example: A defective coherent receiver reports rising errors on one channel even though upstream OSNR and neighbouring channels are normal.

concepts.label: Transmitter wear-out
concepts.gloss: Slow ageing of a terminal's transmit laser, evidenced by increasing bias current and potentially ending in laser failure.
concepts.example: Laser bias climbs to 125% of commissioning value, raising TX-BIAS before the transmitter eventually goes dark.

concepts.label: Margin creep
concepts.gloss: A gradual erosion of a wavelength's reception margin that is observed locally and eventually produces pre-FEC errors or frame loss.
concepts.example: OSNR margin declines by 0.2 dB each month until the receiver begins recording pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: DGD growth
concepts.gloss: An increase in differential group delay somewhere upstream that progressively impairs a wavelength's recoverability.
concepts.example: DGD rises beyond the coherent receiver's tolerance and the terminal first raises DEGRADE and later FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: a polarisation swing
concepts.gloss: A rapid upstream change in optical polarisation that can exceed the receiver tracker's following capability and cause errors.
concepts.example: A fibre disturbance causes fast polarisation rotation, producing bursts of errored seconds at the terminal.

concepts.label: a soiled connector end-face
concepts.gloss: Contamination on an upstream optical connector face that adds loss or noise and degrades the received wavelength.
concepts.example: Cleaning a dirty patch-panel connector restores OSNR and clears the DEGRADE alarm.

concepts.label: transmit laser fault
concepts.gloss: A hardware defect in the local terminal transmitter laser that stops or compromises optical transmission.
concepts.example: The laser driver fails in a VC-WT-400D, causing TX-HW against that terminal's transmitter.

concepts.label: an ODU AIS is arriving
synonyms: an ODU AIS is received on an ODU it switches
concepts.gloss: The tributary is receiving an Optical Data Unit Alarm Indication Signal, signifying an upstream failure and causing AIS propagation and service loss.
concepts.example: A VC-TRIB-100 receives ODU AIS, raises AIS-IN, and forwards AIS on the ODUs it switches.

concepts.label: passes an ODU AIS along on every ODU it switches
concepts.gloss: A cross-connect propagates a received ODU AIS indication onto each downstream ODU affected by its switching operation.
concepts.example: AIS received on an input ODU is emitted on both switched downstream ODU connections.

concepts.label: the ODU arriving is not the expected one
synonyms: receives an ODU meant for someone else
concepts.gloss: The trace identity of a received ODU differs from the ODU provisioned for that tributary, indicating wrong routing.
concepts.example: Tributary A receives tributary B's ODU trace and raises TRACE-MISMATCH.

concepts.label: the customer service on this tributary has failed
concepts.gloss: An end-to-end customer service carried by the specified tributary is unavailable, potentially because of tributary, fabric, ODU, or optical-side failure.
concepts.example: No customer frames pass through VC-TRIB-400, so the port raises urgent TRIB-FAIL.

concepts.label: is set up wrongly
concepts.gloss: A connection's provisioning parameters or switching associations do not implement the intended service path.
concepts.example: The operator maps the client ODU to the wrong cross-connect output during installation.

concepts.label: ends up at the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: A single ODU is delivered to an endpoint other than the one for which it was provisioned.
concepts.example: The London ODU arrives at the Paris tributary because of an incorrect fabric mapping.

concepts.label: the service is dual-homed, with a primary and a standby ODU route
concepts.gloss: The service has two alternative ODU paths, designated primary and standby, for protected delivery.
concepts.example: A customer circuit is provisioned over primary route P and disjoint standby route S.

concepts.label: the selector is at the receiving tributary
concepts.gloss: The protection selector that chooses between primary and standby ODU feeds is located at the receiving tributary endpoint.
concepts.example: The destination VC-TRIB-100 selects whichever of the two incoming ODU routes is healthy.

concepts.label: the standby route is clean
concepts.gloss: The standby ODU route is free of defects and can carry the protected service when selected.
concepts.example: When the primary fails, the standby route has no AIS or frame defects and is immediately usable.

concepts.label: the customer only sees a short interruption while the selector moves
concepts.gloss: A protected service experiences only the brief traffic break needed for its receiving selector to change routes.
concepts.example: After the primary fibre fails, the customer sees a 50 ms interruption while selection moves to standby.

concepts.label: the selector has moved to the standby route
concepts.gloss: The receiving protection selector is currently carrying service from the standby ODU route instead of the primary route.
concepts.example: A primary-route fault causes the tributary to select route S and raise ON-STANDBY.

concepts.label: the standby route has failed
concepts.gloss: The protection route reserved as standby is defective or unavailable, reducing service resilience even if the primary still works.
concepts.example: AIS appears on route S while route P remains active, causing STANDBY-LOST.

concepts.label: tributary hardware fault
concepts.gloss: The tributary port has detected an internal physical equipment defect.
concepts.example: A VC-TRIB-10 interface ASIC fails its self-test and raises TRIB-HW.

concepts.label: fabric hardware fault
concepts.gloss: The digital cross-connect has detected an internal physical defect in its switching fabric.
concepts.example: The VC-DXC reports a failed fabric card and raises FABRIC-HW.

concepts.label: At installation
concepts.gloss: The commissioning phase during which an amplifier's gain is calibrated to offset its feeding fibre span loss and then retained.
concepts.example: At turn-up, a 17 dB span causes the OFA gain to be set and stored at 17 dB.

concepts.label: the gain is set to cancel the attenuation of the fibre length that feeds the module
concepts.gloss: An OFA's configured gain is chosen to equal the attenuation of the fibre span feeding it.
concepts.example: For a measured 14.5 dB incoming span loss, the module is commissioned at 14.5 dB gain.

concepts.label: the module keeps that gain from then on
concepts.gloss: After commissioning, the OFA maintains the configured gain rather than automatically compensating for later input-level changes.
concepts.example: When span loss later increases by 3 dB, the OFA remains at its stored 15 dB gain.

concepts.label: When the incoming light weakens
concepts.gloss: The aggregate optical signal entering a fixed-gain amplifier has fallen in power, causing equally weaker and noisier output wavelengths.
concepts.example: A 2 dB input drop produces a 2 dB output drop and reduced OSNR on all channels.

concepts.label: the outgoing light weakens by the same amount
concepts.gloss: The amplifier output falls by the same power change as its input or gain loss, affecting all wavelengths or a tilted band edge.
concepts.example: Input power drops 3 dB and every output channel also measures 3 dB lower.

concepts.label: every wavelength carried gets noisier
concepts.gloss: All wavelengths traversing the affected amplifier acquire a downstream optical noise penalty.
concepts.example: After an OFA impairment, OSNR falls by 2 dB on every channel measured at the next terminal.

concepts.label: When the incoming light disappears
concepts.gloss: No optical signal reaches a module or terminal receiver, leading to loss of output, loss-of-signal declaration, or OTU frame loss.
concepts.example: A cut span leaves a landing OFA with zero input power and causes IN-DARK.

concepts.label: the outgoing light disappears too
synonyms: no light although light is entering
concepts.gloss: A module emits no aggregate optical output, so every wavelength expected from it is absent.
concepts.example: A failed mid-span OFA receives light but sends none and raises OUT-DARK.

concepts.label: Anything else the module receives
concepts.gloss: Optical traffic received by the module other than the specific failed or discussed signal remains eligible for transparent forwarding.
concepts.example: Unaffected wavelengths entering the module continue through unchanged.

concepts.label: it sends on as it is
concepts.gloss: The module forwards the received signal without terminating or otherwise altering its carried content.
concepts.example: A healthy wavelength entering a line amplifier exits with the same modulation and payload.

concepts.label: Every shelter
concepts.gloss: Each repeater shelter acts as a boundary that terminates the incoming supervisory link and originates a new one on the next span.
concepts.example: Shelter B receives the A–B supervisory channel and starts a separate B–C supervisory channel.

concepts.label: ends the supervisory link it receives
concepts.gloss: A shelter terminates rather than transparently propagates the supervisory communication channel from the preceding fibre span.
concepts.example: The OFA controller consumes the supervisory link received from the upstream shelter.

concepts.label: starts a fresh one on the next fibre length
concepts.gloss: A shelter originates a new supervisory communication link for the following fibre span.
concepts.example: After terminating the west-span link, the shelter launches a new supervisory link eastward.

concepts.label: a supervisory outage
concepts.gloss: The module receives no supervisory-link signal from the fibre span feeding it.
concepts.example: A landing OFA loses its span supervisory channel and raises SV-LOSS.

concepts.label: never spreads beyond the fibre length where it occurs
concepts.gloss: A supervisory-link failure remains confined to its originating fibre span because each shelter regenerates the link.
concepts.example: Loss of the A–B supervisory channel does not interrupt the independently originated B–C channel.

concepts.label: level is fine
concepts.gloss: Measured optical power remains within its expected range even though the signal may have a noise or filtering impairment.
concepts.example: A clipped channel reads -5 dBm as expected but still has a high pre-FEC error ratio.

concepts.label: creeps up
concepts.gloss: The OFA pump-drive indicator I-PUMP rises gradually at the local module as the pump ages.
concepts.example: I-PUMP trends from 100% to 115% over six months.

concepts.label: ends in PUMP-EOL
concepts.gloss: A rising pump-drive trend eventually reaches the threshold that produces the local PUMP-EOL indication.
concepts.example: The trend reaches 121% of commissioning drive and the module raises PUMP-EOL.

concepts.label: no service effect until late
concepts.gloss: The customer service remains operational through most of the component's ageing process and is affected only near final failure.
concepts.example: Traffic remains error-free while pump drive rises to 118%, degrading only shortly before pump failure.

concepts.label: the gain strays more than 2 dB from its setting
concepts.gloss: The measured OFA gain differs from its configured gain by more than 2 dB, satisfying the GAIN-DEV alarm criterion.
concepts.example: A module set for 17 dB delivers 14.6 dB and raises GAIN-DEV.

concepts.label: I-PUMP passes 120 per cent of its commissioning value
concepts.gloss: The current amplifier pump drive exceeds 120% of the value recorded at commissioning.
concepts.example: A pump commissioned at 500 mA reaches 605 mA and triggers PUMP-EOL.

concepts.label: as it leaves a direction
concepts.gloss: The point at which incoming directional optical traffic is separated into individual wavelengths for onward routing.
concepts.example: As the east-direction signal exits the router input stage, each channel is assigned its own output.

concepts.label: The router steers every wavelength on its own.
concepts.gloss: The wavelength router independently selects an onward direction for each constituent wavelength.
concepts.example: Channel 1 is routed north while channel 2 from the same input is routed west.

concepts.label: A problem hits all the light entering on one direction
concepts.gloss: A direction-wide input impairment affects the complete aggregate optical signal arriving at one router direction.
concepts.example: A weak east input reduces the quality of all 40 channels entering from the east.

concepts.label: the problem reappears, after the router, on each wavelength steered onwards from it
concepts.gloss: An input-direction impairment remains present on every affected wavelength after those wavelengths are independently routed onward.
concepts.example: The 40 impaired east-input channels remain noisy across their several output directions.

concepts.label: as long as its attenuation range allows
concepts.gloss: The router can restore wavelength power only while the required correction lies within its supported variable-attenuation range.
concepts.example: The router corrects a 6 dB deficit because its compensation limit is 8 dB.

concepts.label: brings the wavelength levels back to the launch level
synonyms: is evened out at the router
concepts.gloss: The wavelength router equalizes individual channel power to the configured launch level at its output.
concepts.example: Channels arriving between -10 and -5 dBm are all launched onward at -4 dBm.

concepts.label: A drop in level of up to about 8 dB before the router
concepts.gloss: An upstream wavelength power loss no greater than roughly 8 dB remains within the router's level-equalization capability.
concepts.example: A channel arriving 7 dB low is restored to launch power by the router.

concepts.label: the noise penalty the drop caused does not go away
concepts.gloss: Power equalization restores channel level but cannot undo the OSNR degradation caused by an earlier optical power drop.
concepts.example: The router restores a channel to -4 dBm, but its OSNR remains 3 dB below normal.

concepts.label: A bigger drop
concepts.gloss: An upstream wavelength power reduction exceeds the router's available compensation range.
concepts.example: A 12 dB loss reaches a router able to correct only 8 dB.

concepts.label: leaves the router as a weak wavelength
concepts.gloss: One channel exits the wavelength router below its intended launch power because its incoming deficit could not be fully corrected.
concepts.example: After maximum correction, a channel leaves the router 4 dB below target.

concepts.label: crosses the router as it arrived
concepts.gloss: A wavelength traverses the router while retaining the optical impairment it had on arrival.
concepts.example: A noisy channel is switched to a new direction but remains equally noisy.

concepts.label: quality suffers
concepts.gloss: One wavelength has degraded signal integrity despite possibly retaining a normal optical power level.
concepts.example: A passband-clipped channel shows rising pre-FEC errors while its received power remains normal.

concepts.label: stops at the router
concepts.gloss: All optical traffic entering on the failed direction is blocked at the wavelength router.
concepts.example: Failure of the south input prevents every south-originated channel from appearing at any output.

concepts.label: carries on
concepts.gloss: Optical traffic entering the wavelength router through unaffected directions continues to be routed normally.
concepts.example: Channels from north and west remain in service despite failure of the south input.

concepts.label: the terminal declares a loss-of-signal defect (dLOS in G.798 terms)
concepts.gloss: A terminal reports the G.798 dLOS defect after detecting absence of received optical signal.
concepts.example: When received power falls below detection, the VC-WT-400T declares dLOS.

concepts.label: Module failure
concepts.gloss: A terminal module has an equipment-level hardware failure that leads to dEQ declaration and loss of OTU framing.
concepts.example: A failed processor in a VC-WT-200D produces MOD-HW, dEQ, and FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: the terminal declares an equipment defect (dEQ)
concepts.gloss: The terminal reports the G.798 dEQ defect to identify an internal equipment failure.
concepts.example: A failed terminal module causes the local device to declare dEQ.

concepts.label: the OTU frame is lost
synonyms: can no longer find its OTU frame
the frame is lost once it exceeds the margin by far
Once the OTU frame is gone
The OTU frame is lost though light arrives
concepts.gloss: The receiver can no longer recover the Optical Transport Unit frame, causing standards-based downstream AIS insertion and backward defect reporting.
concepts.example: Severe OSNR degradation makes the terminal lose OTU framing and raise FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: Light that arrives in poor shape
concepts.gloss: Received optical light has insufficient signal integrity for reliable decoding, potentially producing pre-FEC errors and eventual frame loss.
concepts.example: A low-OSNR but visible channel accumulates errors and then loses its OTU frame.

concepts.label: weak
concepts.gloss: The received wavelength power is too low for adequate receiver margin.
concepts.example: A channel arrives at -23 dBm, causing pre-FEC errors before frame loss.

concepts.label: noisy
concepts.gloss: The received wavelength has excessive optical noise relative to its signal power.
concepts.example: A channel with 8 dB OSNR produces errors despite normal received power.

concepts.label: with too much differential group delay
concepts.gloss: The received wavelength's differential group delay exceeds the receiver's compensation margin.
concepts.example: DGD reaches 80 ps and the coherent receiver begins losing frames.

concepts.label: clipped by a filter
concepts.gloss: Part of a wavelength's spectrum is removed by a misaligned or narrow optical filter, degrading its decodability.
concepts.example: A router passband clips one modulation sideband and raises the pre-FEC error ratio.

concepts.label: spoiled by the receiver itself
concepts.gloss: Signal degradation is introduced within the local receiver rather than by the optical route.
concepts.example: A faulty receiver DSP creates errors on its channel while another receiver on the same route remains healthy.

concepts.label: The wavelength's margin shrinks slowly
synonyms: with its margin slowly worn away
concepts.gloss: The difference between current wavelength quality and the receiver failure threshold decreases gradually along the route.
concepts.example: A channel's OSNR margin falls from 5 dB to 1 dB over a year before errors appear.

concepts.label: pre-FEC errors begin once the damage exceeds the wavelength's margin
concepts.gloss: The local receiver starts detecting errors before forward-error correction when accumulated impairment exceeds the wavelength's available margin.
concepts.example: Once OSNR drops below the receiver threshold, its pre-FEC error ratio rises from zero.

concepts.label: Polarisation swings faster than the tracker can follow
concepts.gloss: The received state of polarisation changes more rapidly than the terminal's tracking algorithm can compensate.
concepts.example: A mechanical fibre disturbance causes rapid swings and bursts of errored seconds.

concepts.label: errored seconds
concepts.gloss: One or more one-second intervals contain customer traffic errors caused by an optical or receiver impairment.
concepts.example: The terminal records 12 errored seconds during a rapid polarisation event.

concepts.label: the terminal follows G.798
concepts.gloss: After a transport defect, the terminal applies the defect-handling and signal-replacement behaviour specified by ITU-T G.798.
concepts.example: On frame loss, the terminal performs G.798 AIS insertion and backward defect indication.

concepts.label: It inserts ODU AIS towards every ODU it carries downstream
concepts.gloss: A terminal that loses its OTU frame sends ODU AIS downstream on every client ODU carried in that OTU.
concepts.example: Frame loss on an aggregating terminal causes AIS to be inserted into all four downstream ODUs.

concepts.label: returns a backward defect indication to the terminal at the other end
concepts.gloss: The receiving terminal sends a reverse-direction defect indication to inform the transmitting terminal of the forward-path failure.
concepts.example: After losing the forward OTU frame, the receiver reports a backward defect to the far-end terminal.

concepts.label: transmit laser fault
synonyms: The transmit laser stops or fails
concepts.gloss: The transmit laser has stopped or failed sufficiently to compromise the terminal's outgoing wavelength.
concepts.example: A laser driver fault extinguishes the transmitter and causes TX-HW.

concepts.label: loses the wavelength this module sends
concepts.gloss: The remote terminal no longer receives the outgoing wavelength generated by the failed local module.
concepts.example: When the local module fails, the far-end receiver raises RX-DARK for its wavelength.

concepts.label: what the module receives is lost
concepts.gloss: Traffic entering the failed module from the line side is unavailable locally.
concepts.example: A module hardware failure prevents its received ODU from reaching the client interface.

concepts.label: its telemetry stops
concepts.gloss: Management measurements and status reports from the failed module cease on the local side.
concepts.example: After MOD-HW, the controller receives no further power or temperature samples from the module.

concepts.label: its traffic alarms are hidden behind the hardware alarm
concepts.gloss: A module-level hardware alarm suppresses or masks lower-level traffic alarms that would otherwise be reported.
concepts.example: MOD-HW is displayed while subordinate FRAME-LOSS indications from the same module are hidden.

concepts.label: stay healthy
concepts.gloss: Other wavelengths and the shared optical route continue normal operation despite an impairment confined to one receiver.
concepts.example: One receiver reports errors while every neighbouring channel and the route remain healthy.

concepts.label: The laser bias climbs as the laser ages
concepts.gloss: The drive bias required by a transmit laser increases over time as the laser loses efficiency.
concepts.example: Bias rises from 80 mA at commissioning to 98 mA after several years.

concepts.label: it is seen
concepts.gloss: A wavelength-margin change is observable only at the particular receiver measuring that wavelength.
concepts.example: The local terminal reports declining margin while intermediate amplifiers show no anomaly.

concepts.label: Pre-FEC errors exceed the degrade level
concepts.gloss: The measured error ratio before FEC crosses the configured threshold for declaring degraded service.
concepts.example: A pre-FEC ratio of 2×10^-3 exceeds the 1×10^-3 limit and raises DEGRADE.

concepts.label: The other end reports a defect in what this terminal sends
concepts.gloss: The remote terminal sends an indication that the signal transmitted by the local terminal is defective.
concepts.example: A backward defect report from the far end causes the local terminal to raise REMOTE-DEFECT.

concepts.label: Laser bias above 120 per cent of its commissioning value
concepts.gloss: The transmit laser's present bias exceeds 120% of its commissioning baseline, indicating advanced wear.
concepts.example: A laser commissioned at 75 mA reaches 92 mA and raises TX-BIAS.

concepts.label: the other end says it is receiving ODU AIS
concepts.gloss: A remote endpoint reports that the ODU sent toward it is arriving as AIS.
concepts.example: The far tributary reports received AIS, causing the local port to raise REMOTE-AIS.

concepts.label: errored seconds
concepts.gloss: A base telemetry counter of one-second intervals in which the monitored customer or wavelength traffic contained errors.
concepts.example: A tributary port reports 18 errored seconds during the last 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: customer unavailable seconds
concepts.gloss: A base telemetry counter of seconds during which the customer service was classified as unavailable.
concepts.example: A two-minute outage adds 120 customer unavailable seconds at the tributary port.

concepts.label: Aggregate optical power entering the module
concepts.gloss: The total optical power of all wavelengths measured at an OFA's input, available through the Optical Power pack.
concepts.example: A VC-OFA-M reports aggregate input power of +2.4 dBm.

concepts.label: Aggregate optical power leaving the module
concepts.gloss: The total optical power of all wavelengths measured at an OFA's output, available through the Optical Power pack.
concepts.example: A launch OFA reports aggregate output power of +19.0 dBm.

concepts.label: Pump drive, as a share of the value at commissioning
concepts.gloss: An Insight-pack metric expressing current OFA pump drive as a percentage of its commissioning baseline.
concepts.example: A pump-drive reading of 118% shows that the pump needs 18% more drive than at turn-up.

concepts.label: Whether the supervisory link is being received
concepts.gloss: A base status measurement indicating whether a mid-span or landing OFA currently receives its incoming supervisory link.
concepts.example: The landing OFA changes supervisory-link status from received to absent after a span cut.

concepts.label: Received light level
concepts.gloss: The optical power received for a wavelength, obtainable from terminal telemetry and, depending on equipment, base, Optical Power, or Spectrum capability.
concepts.example: A VC-WT-400T reports its channel at -12.3 dBm.

concepts.label: estimated OSNR
concepts.gloss: A per-wavelength estimate of optical signal-to-noise ratio supplied by Spectrum or Insight functionality.
concepts.example: The terminal estimates an OSNR of 14.8 dB for channel 37.

concepts.label: pre-FEC error ratio
concepts.gloss: An Insight-pack measurement of the fraction of received bits found erroneous before forward-error correction.
concepts.example: A terminal reports a pre-FEC error ratio of 4×10^-4.

concepts.label: DGD
concepts.gloss: An Insight-pack measurement of differential group delay on the received optical wavelength.
concepts.example: The receiver reports DGD of 32 ps.

concepts.label: polarisation drift rate
concepts.gloss: An Insight-pack measurement of how rapidly the received optical state of polarisation changes.
concepts.example: The terminal records a drift rate spike during fibre movement.

concepts.label: Transmit laser bias, as a share of its value at commissioning
concepts.gloss: An Insight-pack metric expressing current transmitter laser bias as a percentage of its commissioning value.
concepts.example: A reported laser-bias value of 123% triggers investigation for transmitter ageing.

concepts.label: the digital cross-connect
synonyms: switches ODUs between line modules and tributaries
concepts.gloss: A VC-DXC network element that digitally switches ODUs between line modules and customer tributary ports.
concepts.example: A VC-DXC maps an ODU from a VC-WT-400D line module to a VC-TRIB-400 port.

concepts.label: tributary port
concepts.gloss: A VC-TRIB-10, VC-TRIB-100, or VC-TRIB-400 customer-facing interface that terminates service and measures errored and unavailable seconds.
concepts.example: A VC-TRIB-100 carries a 100G customer service and raises TRIB-FAIL when that service drops.

concepts.label: launch OFA
synonyms: where a wavelength section leaves the wavelength router
concepts.gloss: A VC-OFA-T optical fibre amplifier positioned where a wavelength section leaves a wavelength router, measuring aggregate powers and pump drive.
concepts.example: A VC-OFA-T boosts router output to the section launch level and reports +19 dBm output power.

concepts.label: mid-span OFA
concepts.gloss: A VC-OFA-M line amplifier in a repeater shelter between terminals that measures optical powers, pump drive, and supervisory reception.
concepts.example: A VC-OFA-M in shelter B amplifies the span and raises SV-LOSS when its incoming supervisory link vanishes.

concepts.label: landing OFA
synonyms: where a wavelength section arrives at the next wavelength router
concepts.gloss: A VC-OFA-R amplifier at the receiving end of a wavelength section before the next router, with power, pump, and supervisory monitoring.
concepts.example: A VC-OFA-R boosts light arriving at a router and reports IN-DARK after an upstream fibre cut.

concepts.label: wavelength router
concepts.gloss: A VC-WR-X optical switching resource that independently directs individual wavelengths from incoming directions to selected outgoing directions.
concepts.example: A VC-WR-X sends one east-arriving wavelength north and another west.

concepts.label: single-client wavelength terminal
concepts.gloss: A VC-WT-400T terminal that maps one client service onto one wavelength and monitors optical quality, errors, DGD, polarisation, and laser bias.
concepts.example: A VC-WT-400T transports one 400G client and raises DEGRADE when its pre-FEC errors cross threshold.

concepts.label: aggregating wavelength terminal
concepts.gloss: A VC-WT-200A or VC-WT-400A terminal that aggregates several client services onto one monitored wavelength.
concepts.example: A VC-WT-400A combines four client ODUs onto one line wavelength and measures its OSNR.

concepts.label: digital-switching line module
concepts.gloss: A VC-WT-200D or VC-WT-400D wavelength terminal module interfacing the optical line to digital ODU switching while monitoring line quality.
concepts.example: A VC-WT-400D receives a wavelength, measures pre-FEC errors, and passes its ODUs to the VC-DXC.

concepts.label: TRIB-FAIL
concepts.gloss: An urgent tributary-port alarm indicating failure of the customer service, with possible causes on the route, tributary, provisioning, or switching fabric.
concepts.example: A VC-TRIB-400 raises TRIB-FAIL after a fabric outage cuts its customer service.

concepts.label: AIS-IN
concepts.gloss: An information-only tributary-port alarm indicating that ODU AIS is being received.
concepts.example: A port receiving upstream ODU AIS logs AIS-IN without assigning an urgent local hardware fault.

concepts.label: REMOTE-AIS
concepts.gloss: An information-only tributary-port alarm indicating that the remote endpoint reports receiving ODU AIS from this side.
concepts.example: The far-end tributary reports AIS, so the local port raises REMOTE-AIS.

concepts.label: TRACE-MISMATCH
concepts.gloss: An important tributary-port alarm indicating that the arriving ODU identity is not the provisioned one, usually because of mis-provisioning.
concepts.example: A port expecting trace CLIENT-A receives CLIENT-B and raises TRACE-MISMATCH.

concepts.label: ON-STANDBY
concepts.gloss: An advisory tributary-port alarm indicating that the protection selector is carrying service over the standby route.
concepts.example: A primary-path fault causes switchover and the receiving port raises ON-STANDBY.

concepts.label: STANDBY-LOST
concepts.gloss: An advisory tributary-port alarm indicating that the standby ODU route has failed and protection redundancy is lost.
concepts.example: The primary remains active, but failure of route S raises STANDBY-LOST.

concepts.label: TRIB-HW
concepts.gloss: An urgent tributary-port alarm for a physical hardware fault within the local tributary interface.
concepts.example: A failed VC-TRIB-10 interface circuit raises TRIB-HW.

concepts.label: FABRIC-HW
concepts.gloss: An urgent VC-DXC alarm for a physical hardware fault in the local switching fabric.
concepts.example: A failed cross-connect fabric card raises FABRIC-HW.

concepts.label: IN-DARK
concepts.gloss: An urgent alarm—IN-DARK, SEC-IN-DARK, or RX-DARK—indicating absent incoming light at an OFA or wavelength terminal.
concepts.example: A cut upstream fibre causes a landing OFA to raise SEC-IN-DARK and a terminal to raise RX-DARK.

concepts.label: SV-LOSS
concepts.gloss: An important mid-span or landing OFA alarm indicating loss of the supervisory link on the feeding fibre span.
concepts.example: A severed span prevents supervisory reception and the downstream VC-OFA-M raises SV-LOSS.

concepts.label: OUT-DARK
concepts.gloss: An urgent OFA alarm indicating that no optical light leaves the amplifier, typically because the amplifier is out of service.
concepts.example: A powered-off VC-OFA-T raises OUT-DARK when its output becomes zero.

concepts.label: GAIN-DEV
concepts.gloss: An advisory mid-span or landing OFA alarm indicating gain deviation greater than 2 dB, potentially from outage, sag, or pump wear.
concepts.example: A VC-OFA-R set to 18 dB delivers 15.5 dB and raises GAIN-DEV.

concepts.label: PUMP-EOL
concepts.gloss: An advisory OFA alarm indicating pump drive has exceeded 120% of its commissioning value and the pump is nearing end of life.
concepts.example: A launch OFA reaches 122% pump drive and raises PUMP-EOL.

concepts.label: FRAME-LOSS
concepts.gloss: An urgent wavelength-terminal alarm indicating loss of OTU frame recovery due to severe optical, filtering, DGD, polarisation, or receiver impairment.
concepts.example: Low OSNR prevents a VC-WT-400T from finding its OTU frame, so it raises FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: DEGRADE
concepts.gloss: An advisory wavelength-terminal alarm indicating that the pre-FEC error ratio has exceeded its degradation threshold.
concepts.example: A dirty connector raises the error ratio above threshold and the terminal raises DEGRADE.

concepts.label: REMOTE-DEFECT
concepts.gloss: An information-only terminal alarm indicating that the far end has reported a defect in the signal transmitted by this terminal.
concepts.example: A far-end backward defect indication causes the local VC-WT-200A to raise REMOTE-DEFECT.

concepts.label: TX-HW
concepts.gloss: An urgent terminal alarm identifying a hardware fault in the local transmit laser.
concepts.example: A failed laser in a VC-WT-400D raises TX-HW against its transmitter.

concepts.label: MOD-HW
concepts.gloss: An urgent terminal alarm identifying a hardware failure of the local wavelength module.
concepts.example: A module controller failure on a VC-WT-400T raises MOD-HW and stops telemetry.

concepts.label: TX-BIAS
concepts.gloss: An advisory terminal alarm indicating transmit-laser bias above 120% of its commissioning value, consistent with laser wear-out.
concepts.example: Bias reaches 124% on a VC-WT-200D and TX-BIAS is raised.

concepts.label: The switching fabric
concepts.gloss: The internal ODU switching subsystem of a digital cross-connect considered as the affected extent of a condition.
concepts.example: A service failure is scoped to the switching fabric when tributary and optical interfaces remain healthy.

concepts.label: every ODU
concepts.gloss: All Optical Data Units handled by the affected switching or transport context, rather than one selected ODU.
concepts.example: A fabric outage disrupts every ODU traversing the failed fabric card.

concepts.label: A connection
concepts.gloss: One provisioned logical association between transport endpoints or switching ports.
concepts.example: The wrongly configured cross-connect mapping is confined to a single customer connection.

concepts.label: one ODU
concepts.gloss: A single Optical Data Unit within equipment that may carry many ODUs.
concepts.example: Only ODU CLIENT-A reaches the wrong destination; other ODUs are correct.

concepts.label: the optical side
concepts.gloss: The line-facing optical transport portion of a service path, as distinct from its client-facing interface.
concepts.example: Troubleshooting shows the failure affects the optical side while the tributary electronics pass self-test.

concepts.label: The customer-facing optic
concepts.gloss: The optical transceiver or interface facing the attached customer equipment.
concepts.example: Loss of the customer-facing optic cuts service although the line wavelength remains present.

concepts.label: the tributary itself
concepts.gloss: The specific customer tributary interface and its immediate circuitry.
concepts.example: TRIB-HW affects the tributary itself rather than the shared cross-connect.

concepts.label: the customer service
concepts.gloss: The customer traffic service carried through the tributary and transport network.
concepts.example: A pump can age without affecting the customer service until late in its life.

concepts.label: the module
concepts.gloss: The individual equipment module whose input, output, telemetry, or hardware state is under discussion.
concepts.example: OUT-DARK affects the failed OFA module and all wavelengths leaving it.

concepts.label: every wavelength
concepts.gloss: All optical channels carried through the affected module or aggregate path.
concepts.example: Amplifier excess noise lowers OSNR on every wavelength in the band.

concepts.label: Output levels
concepts.gloss: The set of optical power levels measured at an equipment output.
concepts.example: Output levels remain normal even though excess noise degrades signal quality.

concepts.label: I-PUMP
concepts.gloss: The amplifier pump-drive indicator used to track pump effort relative to commissioning.
concepts.example: Pump wear causes I-PUMP to rise from 100% to 121%.

concepts.label: the trend
concepts.gloss: The time-series progression of a monitored metric rather than a single instantaneous reading.
concepts.example: The pump-drive trend ends at the PUMP-EOL threshold after months of increase.

concepts.label: the wavelengths at one end of the band
concepts.gloss: The subset of optical channels near one spectral edge of the carried band.
concepts.example: Spectral tilt weakens long-wavelength edge channels while central channels remain near target.

concepts.label: one wavelength
concepts.gloss: A single optical channel considered independently of other channels in the same fibre.
concepts.example: A misaligned passband degrades one wavelength while the remaining channels stay healthy.

concepts.label: All the light coming in on that direction
concepts.gloss: The complete aggregate of wavelengths entering a router through one directional input.
concepts.example: An east-input failure blocks all light arriving from the east.

concepts.label: light entering on the other directions
concepts.gloss: Aggregate optical traffic arriving through router inputs other than the affected direction.
concepts.example: North- and west-entering light continues despite failure of the east input.

concepts.label: the transmit laser
concepts.gloss: The optical laser source within a terminal transmitter whose bias and fault state are monitored.
concepts.example: TX-BIAS applies specifically to the transmit laser, not the receiver.

concepts.label: the terminal at the other end of the wavelength
synonyms: the terminal at the other end
concepts.gloss: The remote wavelength endpoint paired with the local terminal over the optical channel.
concepts.example: When the local transmitter fails, the terminal at the other end loses the wavelength.

concepts.label: what the module receives
concepts.gloss: All line-side signal or traffic entering the specified module.
concepts.example: A module failure loses what the module receives before it can reach local clients.

concepts.label: its telemetry
concepts.gloss: The management measurements and status data produced by the specified module.
concepts.example: MOD-HW stops its telemetry, including power and temperature readings.

concepts.label: its traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: The lower-level traffic defect alarms associated with the specified module.
concepts.example: A hardware alarm masks its traffic alarms such as FRAME-LOSS.

concepts.label: this receiver alone
concepts.gloss: Only the particular local optical receiver observing the impairment, excluding the route and other receivers.
concepts.example: A receiver impairment raises pre-FEC errors on this receiver alone.

concepts.label: the other wavelengths
concepts.gloss: All wavelength channels sharing the route except the specifically impaired channel.
concepts.example: The other wavelengths remain healthy when one receiver is defective.

concepts.label: the route
concepts.gloss: The optical path traversed by the wavelength between its endpoints.
concepts.example: A local receiver fault leaves the route itself healthy.

concepts.label: transmitter
concepts.gloss: The complete terminal transmit function, including its laser and supporting electronics.
concepts.example: A transmit-laser fault affects the transmitter while reception can continue.

concepts.label: the wavelength's margin
concepts.gloss: The remaining tolerance between a wavelength's current received quality and the threshold at which errors or frame loss begin.
concepts.example: The wavelength's margin shrinks from 4 dB to 0.5 dB as OSNR deteriorates.

concepts.label: this cross-connect
concepts.gloss: The local digital cross-connect through which the affected ODU is switched or against which a fabric issue is reported.
concepts.example: FABRIC-HW is reported against this cross-connect, VC-DXC-7.

concepts.label: on the ODU route in use
concepts.gloss: Some point on the currently selected end-to-end ODU path carrying the service.
concepts.example: TRIB-FAIL may be caused by a fault on the ODU route in use between sites A and B.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: At either of the two endpoint tributaries or terminals bounding the service.
concepts.example: The tributary fault is found at the remote end rather than the local end.

concepts.label: at a cross-connect along the ODU route
concepts.gloss: At an intermediate or endpoint digital cross-connect traversed by the ODU path.
concepts.example: A mis-provisioned mapping at the second cross-connect sends the ODU to the wrong tributary.

concepts.label: the customer service on this tributary
concepts.gloss: The service instance carried through the specified customer-facing tributary, used as an alarm reporting object.
concepts.example: TRIB-FAIL is reported against the 100G service on tributary port 3.

concepts.label: the ODU arriving
concepts.gloss: The incoming ODU at the receiving tributary where its identity or trace is checked.
concepts.example: TRACE-MISMATCH is reported against the ODU arriving on port 8.

concepts.label: on the primary route
concepts.gloss: At some element or span of the ODU path designated as the normal protected-service route.
concepts.example: A fibre fault on the primary route causes selection of standby.

concepts.label: the selector
concepts.gloss: The receiving protection-selection function that chooses between primary and standby ODU inputs.
concepts.example: ON-STANDBY is reported against the selector after it chooses route S.

concepts.label: the standby route
concepts.gloss: The alternative ODU path reserved to protect the primary route.
concepts.example: STANDBY-LOST is reported against the standby route while primary traffic continues.

concepts.label: this tributary
concepts.gloss: The local customer-facing tributary interface identified by the alarm or diagnosis.
concepts.example: TRIB-HW is reported against this tributary, VC-TRIB-100 port 2.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: At points following the affected component in the direction of optical signal travel.
concepts.example: Noise added by a mid-span OFA is visible at all downstream terminals.

concepts.label: this module
concepts.gloss: The local equipment module currently being monitored or diagnosed.
concepts.example: PUMP-EOL is raised on this module, the VC-OFA-M in shelter 12.

concepts.label: the fibre length feeding the module
concepts.gloss: The immediately preceding fibre span that delivers light and supervisory signalling to the module.
concepts.example: SV-LOSS points to the 80 km fibre length feeding the landing OFA.

concepts.label: the OFA before that fibre length
concepts.gloss: The upstream optical fibre amplifier that launches light into the span feeding the current module.
concepts.example: An outage of the preceding OFA leaves the downstream module dark.

concepts.label: the patch lead at the head of the wavelength section
concepts.gloss: The short optical jumper at the launch end of a wavelength section before its first fibre span.
concepts.example: An unplugged patch lead at the section head causes all downstream receivers to see darkness.

concepts.label: the router
concepts.gloss: The wavelength-routing node at which channel steering, equalization, or direction-input failure is observed.
concepts.example: A weak channel is measured as leaving the router below launch target.

concepts.label: the other end of the wavelength
concepts.gloss: The remote terminal endpoint of the same bidirectional wavelength connection.
concepts.example: A dark transmitter at the other end causes no light at the local receiver.

concepts.label: on this side
concepts.gloss: At the local endpoint or equipment side from which the condition is being described.
concepts.example: A module failure stops telemetry on this side while the far end loses the transmitted wavelength.

concepts.label: this receiver alone
concepts.gloss: At the particular local receiver where an impairment or error symptom is observed and nowhere else.
concepts.example: Pre-FEC errors appear at this receiver alone despite healthy route telemetry.

concepts.label: along its route
concepts.gloss: At one or more points on the end-to-end path traversed by the wavelength.
concepts.example: The wavelength accumulates gradual margin loss along its route.

concepts.label: anywhere earlier on the wavelength's route
concepts.gloss: At any upstream point traversed by the wavelength before the current observation location.
concepts.example: A dirty connector anywhere earlier on the route can cause the terminal's DEGRADE alarm.

concepts.label: this terminal
concepts.gloss: The local wavelength terminal containing the receiver or transmitter under diagnosis.
concepts.example: TX-BIAS is reported against this terminal, VC-WT-400T-5.

concepts.label: between here and the other end, the other end included
concepts.gloss: Anywhere on the complete path from the local observation point through and including the remote endpoint.
concepts.example: REMOTE-DEFECT may reflect a fault between the local terminal and the far terminal, including the far terminal itself.

concepts.label: what this terminal sends
concepts.gloss: The locally transmitted optical signal or payload as evaluated by the remote endpoint.
concepts.example: REMOTE-DEFECT is reported against what this terminal sends after the far end detects errors.

concepts.label: This terminal's transmitter
concepts.gloss: The local terminal's optical transmit subsystem, including its laser, used as the reporting location for transmit faults.
concepts.example: TX-HW is reported against this terminal's transmitter rather than its receiver.

concepts.label: Base
concepts.gloss: The standard telemetry entitlement supplied without an optional monitoring pack.
concepts.example: A tributary's errored-seconds counter is available under Base capability.

concepts.label: Optical Power pack
concepts.gloss: An optional capability pack that exposes aggregate and received optical power measurements.
concepts.example: Enabling the Optical Power pack adds OFA input and output power telemetry.

concepts.label: Insight pack
concepts.gloss: An optional advanced diagnostics pack exposing health and signal-quality metrics such as pump drive, OSNR, pre-FEC ratio, DGD, polarisation, and laser bias.
concepts.example: With Insight enabled, a terminal reports pre-FEC error ratio and laser bias percentage.

concepts.label: With the Spectrum pack
concepts.gloss: Availability of per-wavelength level and OSNR measurements when the optional Spectrum pack is installed.
concepts.example: After enabling the Spectrum pack, operators can view channel 37's power and estimated OSNR.

concepts.label: An outage
synonyms: An outage; it happens mostly straight after provisioning work.
concepts.gloss: A failure mode involving complete loss of a component, path, signal, or service rather than merely reduced quality.
concepts.example: A fabric card failure completely cuts an ODU service and is classified as an outage.

concepts.label: A degradation
concepts.gloss: A failure mode in which service or signal quality is impaired but not necessarily absent.
concepts.example: Gain sag lowers power and OSNR while traffic may still pass, so it is a degradation.

concepts.label: Slow
concepts.gloss: A progressive failure nature that develops gradually over time rather than occurring abruptly.
concepts.example: Pump wear raises drive current over months before reaching PUMP-EOL.

concepts.label: urgent
concepts.gloss: The highest operational priority used for conditions causing or strongly indicating immediate service or equipment failure.
concepts.example: FRAME-LOSS is urgent because the terminal can no longer recover the OTU frame.

concepts.label: information only
concepts.gloss: A non-action-priority classification that records remote or propagated status for operator awareness.
concepts.example: AIS-IN is information only because it reports an upstream indication rather than a local hardware failure.

concepts.label: important
concepts.gloss: A significant alarm priority requiring attention but below urgent service-failure severity.
concepts.example: SV-LOSS is important because span supervision is lost even if payload light remains.

concepts.label: advisory
concepts.gloss: A warning classification for reduced resilience, degradation, or ageing that does not necessarily cause current service loss.
concepts.example: PUMP-EOL is advisory because the amplifier may still carry traffic while its pump approaches end of life.

concepts.label: dual-homed, with a primary and a standby ODU route and the selector at the receiving tributary
concepts.gloss: A protection behaviour in which a service reaches a receiving tributary over primary and standby ODU routes and a local selector chooses the usable feed.
concepts.example: When route P fails and route S is clean, the receiving selector switches to S with only a brief customer interruption.

concepts.label: The router steers every wavelength on its own as it leaves a direction.
concepts.gloss: A wavelength-routing behaviour in which each channel from an incoming direction is independently switched to its configured outgoing direction.
concepts.example: From one eastbound aggregate, the router sends channel 21 north and channel 22 south.
